proposal: The Mandate says the next Administration should extend the African Growth and Opportunity Act, which gives eligible African countries duty-free access to US markets, beyond its 2025 expiration, but within a strategic framework that rewards good governance and pro-market economic policies rather than channeling benefits to governments that fail to reform.

source_checks.note: Approved 2026-09-02. Section 2008 changes 2026 to 2028 in Trade Act section 506B and AGOA section 112(g), sets the regional apparel program to run each year until 2028-12-31, and moves the third-country fabric dates to 2028; no separate effective date, no conditions, no link to the 2026-12-11 continuing-appropriations end date, and no new eligibility criteria.

Proclamation 11030, signed 2026-05-19, published 2026-05-22 (91 FR 30469), implements P.L. 119-75 section 5019: AGOA preferences, the regional apparel program and the third-country fabric program remain in effect through 2026-12-31; designates Gabon effective 2026-01-01; does not itself state retroactivity.

significance.rationale: Extending AGOA continues duty-free access for African imports with marginal effect for US consumers and firms.

status_summary: AGOA's prior authorization expired on 2025-09-30. Public Law 119-75 (the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, enacted 2026-02-03) reauthorized it through 2026-12-31 retroactive to the expiration, and Proclamation 11030 (signed 2026-05-19) implemented the extension and designated Gabon as a beneficiary effective 2026-01-01. Public Law 119-103, the Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027 (enacted 2026-09-02), then changed the 2026 dates for AGOA's main provisions to 2028 in its Section 2008. On the framework element, USTR published a request for comments on modernizing AGOA on 2026-04-29 (136 comments received), asking about eligibility criteria, graduation, reciprocity and enforcement to inform recommendations to Congress, and on 2026-06-30 began the annual country eligibility review for 2027 under the program's existing criteria. No legislation changing those criteria was found, so the extension is in law but the strategic-framework element remains at the recommendation stage.

timeline.event: AGOA's prior authorization expires, according to USTR's later notice.

Public Law 119-75 (Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, H.R. 7148) is enacted; the GovInfo public law page dates it 2026-02-03. USTR's 2026-04-29 notice (below) describes it as reauthorizing AGOA through 2026-12-31, retroactive to 2025-09-30.

USTR publishes a request for comments on modernizing AGOA to inform recommendations to Congress, covering eligibility criteria, graduation, reciprocity, critical minerals supply chains and enforcement; comments closed 2026-05-15 with 136 received.

Proclamation 11030 (published 2026-05-22) implements the AGOA extension through 2026-12-31, including the regional apparel and third-country fabric programs, and designates Gabon as a beneficiary effective 2026-01-01.

USTR opens its annual review of country eligibility for AGOA for calendar year 2027, conditioned on reauthorization, applying criteria that include a market-based economy, rule of law, anti-corruption systems and worker rights, with a public hearing on 2026-07-23.

Public Law 119-103 (Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027) is enacted; its Section 2008 changes the 2026 dates in AGOA's termination provision, regional apparel program and third-country fabric program to 2028 and sets the apparel program's end at 2028-12-31. The text states no new eligibility conditions.

title: Extend AGOA past 2025 within a framework that rewards good governance
uncertainties: Public Law 119-75's AGOA text was not read directly; the 2026-02-03 reauthorization and its retroactivity come from USTR's 2026-04-29 notice. Section 2008 of Public Law 119-103 was read through a fetch summary, which reported that each 2026 reference becomes 2028 and that no effective-date clause or new conditions appear; the exact statutory end date of the main provision (beyond the apparel program's 2028-12-31 end) was not confirmed. The eligibility-review notice has an internal conflict on the testimony deadline (2026-07-09 versus 2026-07-13). Congress's role in modernizing AGOA and any pending reform bill were not searched. The Mandate does not define the strategic framework, so the match between existing eligibility criteria and the Mandate's good-governance condition is a judgment.
